title: Iterative intake spec and negotiable pinning for community/open models
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Clarify and formalize requirements for onboarding new open/community model weights into the Redwood model catalog when the intake is expected to be iterative. This ticket defines a negotiation flow for 'soft pin' semantics, explicit compatibility notes that runtime engineers and the serving runtime can consume, the minimum metadata that the model submitter must provide, and acceptance criteria for staged rollouts. The goal is to reduce back-and-forth between PM/Runtime/Onboarding engineers while preserving safety and runtime reliability. Key focus areas: 1) precise metadata contract for compatibility signals (tokenizer id, kv-cache layout, supported sequence lengths, quantization artifacts), 2) semantics for soft pin vs hard pin and rollback triggers, 3) staged canary rollout checklist and eval thresholds, and 4) documentation templates and automation hooks to gate entry. This is intended to replace ad-hoc email/PR workflows with a predictable intake flow that supports iterative model updates without impacting customer workloads.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable intake template is approved and published (YAML/JSON) listing required fields: model_id, architecture, tokenizer_spec, kv_cache_compat, sequence_length_limits, quantization_profile, recommended runtime variant, and provenance links.

Definition of 'soft pin' vs 'hard pin' documented with concrete runtime behaviors: soft pin allows automatic fallback to a compatible variant; hard pin blocks fallback and requires explicit infrastructure approval.
Compatibility note schema v1 is implemented in the intake template and mapped to runtime flags (e.g., kv_cache_layout: v0|v1, attention_chunking: supported|unknown).

Canary rollout checklist created with measurable gates: perf baseline (<=10% tail-latency regression), quality regression check (evaluations on seed prompt set: pass rate >= 95% relative to canonical model), and error-rate threshold (<0.5% increase).

Automation: Onboarding submission creates a checklist issue with links to eval run, PRs, and a staging model endpoint; runtime team can opt-in to auto-run sanity suite; failures produce actionable errors.
Operator rollback policy documented: automatic rollback triggers when canary error-rate or latency breaches gate; manual override path and owner contact included.
Two intake examples (one small open model, one larger community weight with quantized artifacts) included in the published doc.
Onboarding workflow reduces average triage turnaround time for community model submissions by 30% in pilot phase (tracked via Linear metrics).

notes: Trade-offs: More required metadata reduces friction for runtime but increases burden on submitters. We will pilot with a reduced required set and suggest optional heuristics for advanced signals.
Fallback semantics must be conservative for enterprise customers with reserved capacity; consider flagging 'enterprise-impact' models during intake.
Consider adding a lightweight verification signing step for provenance (commit hash + model checksum) to prevent accidental mismatches during iterative uploads.
